question: Which statement is Lenz's Law?
choices: The direction of an induced current is such that it opposes the change in magnetic flux that produced it.
The direction of an induced current is always the same as the direction of the magnetic field.
An induced current always flows clockwise when seen from the magnet.
An induced current only flows when the magnetic flux stays constant.
explanation: Lenz's Law: the induced current flows in the direction that **opposes the change in magnetic flux** that produced it.

question: Lenz's Law is named after the physicist who formulated it. Who was he, and in what year did he state it?
explanation: The law is named after **Heinrich Friedrich Emil Lenz**, who formulated it in **1834**. Faraday discovered electromagnetic induction in 1831; Lenz described the direction of the induced current.

question: The opposition described by Lenz's Law is a result of which fundamental principle?
explanation: The opposition is a manifestation of the **conservation of energy**. You must do work against the opposing force, and that work becomes electrical energy.

question: In Faraday's Law, $\varepsilon = -N\dfrac{\Delta \Phi}{\Delta t}$, what does the negative sign show?
choices: The induced EMF opposes the change in magnetic flux.
The induced EMF is always a negative number.
The number of turns decreases with time.
explanation: The negative sign is how **Lenz's Law** enters Faraday's Law: the induced EMF acts to **oppose the change** in flux. It does not mean the EMF is always negative.

question: Which situation induces NO current in a closed loop of wire?
choices: A magnet is pushed into the loop.
The magnetic field through the loop gets stronger.
The loop is rotated inside a magnetic field.
A magnet rests beside the loop and neither of them moves.
explanation: An EMF is induced only when the **magnetic flux changes**: by motion, by a changing field strength, or by a changing orientation. A magnet at rest beside the loop gives **constant flux**, so there is no current.

question: The magnetic flux through a loop is decreasing. Which way does the induced magnetic field point inside the loop?
choices: The same direction as the original field
Parallel to the plane of the loop
explanation: The induced field opposes the **change**. When the flux decreases, the induced field points the **same way** as the original field to try to keep the flux from dropping.

question: In the right-hand rule for a coil or solenoid, the fingers curl along the current. What does the thumb point to?
choices: The south pole of the coil
The direction of the current in one wire
The magnetic field inside the coil, which is its north pole
explanation: For a coil: **fingers curl along the current**, and the **thumb** points along the **field inside the coil**, which is the coil's **north pole**.

question: The north pole of a bar magnet is moved **toward** a loop of wire. What pole does the induced current create on the side of the loop facing the magnet?
choices: Both poles on the same side
explanation: The flux from the N pole **increases**, so the loop opposes it by making a **north pole** on the side facing the magnet. Like poles **repel**, which opposes the approach.

question: The north pole of a bar magnet is pulled away from a loop of wire. Which statement correctly describes the loop's induced magnetic field?
choices: A north pole faces the magnet and repels it.
A south pole faces the magnet and repels it.
No field forms, because the magnet is moving.
A south pole faces the magnet and attracts it.
explanation: The induced field opposes the change. A receding magnet is **attracted** back, so the face toward it is the opposite pole: a **south pole** that **attracts** the magnet. Like poles repel and unlike poles attract, so a south pole could never repel a north pole.

question: The south pole of a bar magnet is pushed toward a loop of wire. Which statement correctly describes the loop's induced magnetic field?
choices: A south pole faces the magnet and repels it.
A north pole faces the magnet and attracts it.
A south pole faces the magnet and attracts it.
No field forms, because the magnet is moving.
explanation: The induced field opposes the change. An approaching magnet is **repelled**, so the face toward it is the same pole as the magnet: a **south pole** that **repels** the magnet. Like poles repel and unlike poles attract, so a south pole could never attract a south pole.

question: The magnet moves as shown. Which way does the induced current flow on the front of the coil (the side facing you)?
figure: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="-6 -6 302 157" width="302" height="157" role="img" aria-label="A bar magnet on the right of a coil, with its N pole facing the coil, moving toward the coil" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"><ellipse cx="40" cy="80" rx="9" ry="42"/><ellipse cx="56" cy="80" rx="9" ry="42"/><ellipse cx="72" cy="80" rx="9" ry="42"/><ellipse cx="88" cy="80" rx="9" ry="42"/><ellipse cx="104" cy="80" rx="9" ry="42"/><line x1="40" y1="122" x2="40" y2="140"/><line x1="104" y1="122" x2="104" y2="140"/><text x="72" y="14" font-size="12" text-anchor="middle" dominant-baseline="central" fill="currentColor" stroke="none" font-style="italic">coil</text><rect x="160" y="62" width="110" height="36"/><line x1="215" y1="62" x2="215" y2="98"/><text x="187.5" y="80" font-size="16" text-anchor="middle" dominant-baseline="central" fill="currentColor" stroke="none" font-weight="bold">N</text><text x="242.5" y="80" font-size="16" text-anchor="middle" dominant-baseline="central" fill="currentColor" stroke="none" font-weight="bold">S</text><polyline points="239,46 191,46"/><polygon points="191,46 199.1,42.09 199.1,49.91" fill="currentColor" stroke-width="1"/><text x="215" y="30" font-size="14" text-anchor="middle" dominant-baseline="central" fill="currentColor" stroke="none" font-style="italic">v</text></svg>
explanation: Field lines **leave** the N pole, so at the coil $B$ points to the **left**. The magnet moves toward the coil, so this flux **increases**. The induced field must oppose it: it points to the **right**, so the coil's face toward the magnet is a **north pole** (it repels the approaching magnet). Right-hand rule for a coil: thumb to the right, and the current on the front of the coil flows **down**.

question: The magnet moves as shown. Which way does the induced current flow on the front of the coil (the side facing you)?
figure: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="-6 -6 302 157" width="302" height="157" role="img" aria-label="A bar magnet on the right of a coil, with its S pole facing the coil, moving toward the coil" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"><ellipse cx="40" cy="80" rx="9" ry="42"/><ellipse cx="56" cy="80" rx="9" ry="42"/><ellipse cx="72" cy="80" rx="9" ry="42"/><ellipse cx="88" cy="80" rx="9" ry="42"/><ellipse cx="104" cy="80" rx="9" ry="42"/><line x1="40" y1="122" x2="40" y2="140"/><line x1="104" y1="122" x2="104" y2="140"/><text x="72" y="14" font-size="12" text-anchor="middle" dominant-baseline="central" fill="currentColor" stroke="none" font-style="italic">coil</text><rect x="160" y="62" width="110" height="36"/><line x1="215" y1="62" x2="215" y2="98"/><text x="187.5" y="80" font-size="16" text-anchor="middle" dominant-baseline="central" fill="currentColor" stroke="none" font-weight="bold">S</text><text x="242.5" y="80" font-size="16" text-anchor="middle" dominant-baseline="central" fill="currentColor" stroke="none" font-weight="bold">N</text><polyline points="239,46 191,46"/><polygon points="191,46 199.1,42.09 199.1,49.91" fill="currentColor" stroke-width="1"/><text x="215" y="30" font-size="14" text-anchor="middle" dominant-baseline="central" fill="currentColor" stroke="none" font-style="italic">v</text></svg>

The induced field must oppose it: it points to the **left**, so the coil's face toward the magnet is a **south pole** (it repels the approaching magnet). Right-hand rule for a coil: thumb to the left, and the current on the front of the coil flows **up**.

The induced field must keep it: it points to the **left**, so the coil's face toward the magnet is a **north pole** (it attracts the receding magnet). Right-hand rule for a coil: thumb to the left, and the current on the front of the coil flows **up**.

question: A square loop lies in a uniform magnetic field directed into the page. The field strength is **decreasing**. What is the direction of the induced current in the loop?
choices: It alternates between CW and ACW
explanation: Original flux: **into the page**, decreasing. The induced field must make up for the decrease, so it points **into the page**. Right-hand rule for a coil: thumb into the page, fingers curl **clockwise**.

question: A circular loop lies in a uniform magnetic field directed into the page. The field strength is **increasing**. What is the direction of the induced current in the loop?
choices: It alternates between CW and ACW
explanation: Original flux: **into the page**, increasing. The induced field must oppose the increase, so it points **out of the page**. Right-hand rule for a coil: thumb out of the page, fingers curl **anticlockwise**.

question: A long straight wire carries an upward current that is **decreasing**. A circular loop lies to the right of the wire. What is the direction of the induced current in the loop?
figure: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="-6 -6 262 152" width="262" height="152" role="img" aria-label="A long straight wire with an upward current that is decreasing, and a circular loop to the right of the wire" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"><polyline points="40,130 40,10"/><polygon points="40,10 44.35,19 35.65,19" fill="currentColor" stroke-width="1"/><text x="26" y="70" font-size="14" text-anchor="middle" dominant-baseline="central" fill="currentColor" stroke="none" font-style="italic">I</text><circle cx="130" cy="70" r="38"/><text x="182" y="108.2" font-size="13" text-anchor="start" dominant-baseline="central" fill="currentColor" stroke="none" font-style="italic"><tspan x="182" y="108.2">I is</tspan><tspan x="182" y="123.8">decreasing</tspan></text></svg>
explanation: Right-hand rule for a straight wire: thumb up, fingers curl so that on the **right** side the field points **into the page**. The current is decreasing, so this flux is **decreasing**. The induced field points **into the page**, so the induced current is **clockwise**.

question: A long straight wire carries a downward current that is **decreasing**. A circular loop lies to the left of the wire. What is the direction of the induced current in the loop?
figure: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="-6 -6 302 152" width="302" height="152" role="img" aria-label="A long straight wire with a downward current that is decreasing, and a circular loop to the left of the wire" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"><polyline points="200,10 200,130"/><polygon points="200,130 195.65,121 204.35,121" fill="currentColor" stroke-width="1"/><text x="214" y="70" font-size="14" text-anchor="middle" dominant-baseline="central" fill="currentColor" stroke="none" font-style="italic">I</text><circle cx="110" cy="70" r="38"/><text x="4" y="108.2" font-size="13" text-anchor="start" dominant-baseline="central" fill="currentColor" stroke="none" font-style="italic"><tspan x="4" y="108.2">I is</tspan><tspan x="4" y="123.8">decreasing</tspan></text></svg>
explanation: Right-hand rule for a straight wire: thumb down, fingers curl so that on the **left** side the field points **into the page**. The current is decreasing, so this flux is **decreasing**. The induced field points **into the page**, so the induced current is **clockwise**.

question: The outer loop carries an anticlockwise current that is **increasing**. Which statement correctly describes the induced current in the inner loop?
figure: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="-6 -6 252 172" width="252" height="172" role="img" aria-label="Two concentric loops. The outer loop carries a anticlockwise current that is increasing" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"><circle cx="80" cy="80" r="62"/><circle cx="80" cy="80" r="28"/><path d="M119.85 32.51 A62 62 0 0 0 32.51 40.15"/><polygon points="32.51,40.15 35.02,31.51 40.84,36.74" fill="currentColor" stroke-width="1"/><text x="162" y="44.4" font-size="13" text-anchor="start" dominant-baseline="central" fill="currentColor" stroke="none" font-style="italic"><tspan x="162" y="44.4">outer:</tspan><tspan x="162" y="60">ACW,</tspan><tspan x="162" y="75.6">increasing</tspan></text><text x="162" y="128" font-size="13" text-anchor="start" dominant-baseline="central" fill="currentColor" stroke="none" font-style="italic">inner: ?</text></svg>
choices: ACW, since flux out of the page increases
CW, since flux out of the page increases
CW, since flux into the page increases
ACW, since the inner loop always copies the outer loop
explanation: Right-hand rule: an anticlockwise current makes a field **out of the page**. Inside the outer loop the field points **out of the page**, so the inner loop has flux out of the page. The current is increasing, so this flux increases. The induced field points **into the page**, so the inner loop's current is **clockwise (CW)**.

question: The inner loop carries a clockwise current that is **increasing**. What is the direction of the induced current in the outer loop?
figure: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="-6 -6 252 172" width="252" height="172" role="img" aria-label="Two concentric loops. The inner loop carries a clockwise current that is increasing" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"><circle cx="80" cy="80" r="62"/><circle cx="80" cy="80" r="28"/><path d="M55.75 66.00 A28 28 0 0 1 101.45 62.00"/><polygon points="101.45,62 93.12,58.6 98.94,53.36" fill="currentColor" stroke-width="1"/><text x="162" y="44.4" font-size="13" text-anchor="start" dominant-baseline="central" fill="currentColor" stroke="none" font-style="italic"><tspan x="162" y="44.4">inner:</tspan><tspan x="162" y="60">CW,</tspan><tspan x="162" y="75.6">increasing</tspan></text><text x="162" y="128" font-size="13" text-anchor="start" dominant-baseline="central" fill="currentColor" stroke="none" font-style="italic">outer: ?</text></svg>
choices: The same as the inner loop, always
explanation: Right-hand rule: a clockwise current makes a field **into the page**. The inner loop's field points **into the page** inside it. Most of the field through the outer loop is this strong field near the center, so the net flux through the outer loop is also **into the page**. The current is increasing, so this flux increases. The induced field points **out of the page**, so the outer loop's current is **anticlockwise (ACW)**.
